text.receiving_and_sorting_use: Receiving and Sorting use your own goods, not scanned: put out boxes to receive, and the teams sort what they bring in. Prepare Training adds offers for those deliveries to match. The goods that start out already in the warehouse — the sorting area table, sealed trays at the table spots with orders to pick, and picked orders to ship (Stations 3–5) — are the ones you scan first, so the system knows exactly what is there. Each team also gets a driver. After its first station every team works on the goods it handled one station earlier. The setup packet says which scanned goods go at which spot or in which load, with a contents slip for each and a sign for each station.

text.a_printer_is_only: A printer is only offered in Print menus once it has a site and a paper type and is switched on. Changing a paper type needs the printer's queue to be empty.

text.a_weekly_backup_also: A weekly backup also counts as that day's daily one. Backups made by hand and the ones taken before an upgrade are not deleted by this schedule (the upgrade ones go after the usual number of days). These sit on this machine: copy them elsewhere too (the RI Launcher can). The provisioner works on one request at a time, so creating a warehouse waits while a big backup runs.

text.just_as_important_every: Just as important: every warehouse and every incident is not the same. A small volunteer-run site and a large multi-agency distribution point don't operate identically, and a tool that forces both into one rigid workflow ends up fighting the people using it. The goal here is flexibility by design — configurable enough that a warehouse manager's real process shapes how the software behaves, rather than the other way around.

text.relief_inventory_began_during: Relief Inventory began during the response to Hurricane Helene in Western North Carolina. A disaster relief warehouse needed a way to track incoming donations accurately and quickly, route approval decisions, and manage outgoing shipments — and nothing on the market fit the unique needs of a donations warehouse. A Google Sheets system was cobbled together to keep pace, then reworked again and again as the situation evolved. Its limitations soon became clear, and work began on something better — starting not with a spec, but with a meeting of the minds among the people actually running the warehouse. Out of that collaboration, a framework began to take shape: one meant to guide a donation all the way from the initial offer through delivery to a distribution point, while tracking volunteer hours along the way.
text.relief_inventory_is_a: Relief Inventory is a warehouse management system for disaster relief. It tracks donated goods from the moment they arrive, through sorting onto shelves and pallets, to the orders that partner organizations request and the shipments that fill them.

text.that_collaboration_has_continued: That collaboration has continued ever since, alongside Adventist Community Services and the volunteers and staff who use the system day to day. The software has been shaped less by a spec written in advance and more by real operations — it went into use while it was still being built, and most of what exists today — from how sorting sessions autosave line-by-line so a dropped connection never loses a scan, to how an order moves through filling, shipping, and delivery — traces back to a specific gap someone hit while the work was happening, not a feature that sounded good on paper.

That's necessary, but on its own it's just a database — and a database doesn't help a new volunteer figure out what to do next, doesn't remember why a donation needs a second look, and doesn't adapt when two warehouses run their operations differently for good reasons.

text.turn_this_on_when: Turn this on when this warehouse has no reliable internet connection. It automatically disables Cloudflare Turnstile (bot protection on login/registration/password reset) and geocod.io address lookups (county/city/state auto-fill on Order Entry and People) — neither is required for normal operation, they just fail slowly without a real network otherwise. Nothing else changes — address, order, and inventory entry all work exactly the same either way.
